title: Domino Wonder Dash
one_line: Trace real outlines, topple dominoes, play Find it!, Spell it and daily stories: ABC, Hindi letters, numbers, animals, maps and more, in English with Hindi or Bangla.
how_to_play: Tap once to start. Trace the dots with your finger or mouse, then tap to topple the dominoes. The first tap also goes full screen (wide screens get a big landscape layout). The red play button shows a short real video of the picture, then Back to play. The Games button opens Find it!, Spell it, Draw my own (free drawing with crayon colours that becomes dominoes), Story of the day, players, language, a parents report and the full screen switch.
description: A learning game for children at NCERT Class 1 to 5 level. Every item has a real dotted outline to trace over a faint picture: A to Z and a to z, the Hindi varnamala (swar and vyanjan, spoken in Hindi where the device has a Hindi voice), numbers, maths signs and shapes, animals, birds, sea life, reptiles, insects, plants, fruits, vegetables, food, body parts, homes and buildings, community helpers, vehicles, bridges, sky and weather, countries on India's official map, the whole India map plus all 28 states and 8 union territories with their capitals and famous places (Delhi shows the National War Memorial, India Gate, Red Fort, Qutub Minar and more), 11 Indian monuments, famous city landmarks and real rivers, plus cartoon friends such as a superhero, robot, unicorn, dragon, fairy and mermaid. When the outline is traced, dominoes stand up on it; tap and they topple, the real picture appears and the name is said, spelled and shown. Sparks fly from every dot, quick tracing builds a musical streak, five colour themes, and a sticker shelf rewards milestones and finished categories. The Games button adds a picture quiz (Find it!), a spelling game, 14 short stories, up to six child profiles, every name in Hindi or Bangla, and a progress report for parents. Real sounds (animal calls, vehicles, instruments, rain) play after each picture. Works with a finger on phones and tablets or with a mouse. Pictures: OpenMoji (CC BY-SA 4.0); maps: Natural Earth.
